definition: A family of models formulated so they train in parallel like transformers but run as RNNs at inference, with constant memory per token and no KV cache.
details: A family of models formulated so they train in parallel like transformers but run as RNNs at inference, with constant memory per token and no KV cache. The flagship community-driven attention-free lineage, notable for strong multilingual open releases.

explainer.lead: RWKV is a family of models formulated so they train in parallel like transformers but run as RNNs at inference, with constant memory per token and no KV cache. It matters as a flagship community-driven attention-free lineage with notable strong multilingual open releases.

tiers.eli5: It trains the way most modern models do, but when answering it reads one word at a time with a fixed-size memory instead of keeping a growing scratchpad.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to get transformer-style parallel training while keeping constant per-token inference memory without a KV cache; the attention-free design means the usual KV-cache tooling does not apply.
tiers.paperLevel: Models trained in parallel like transformers but executed as RNNs at inference, with constant memory per token and no KV cache; the lineage is attention-free. Limits: constant-memory recurrence constrains what the model can retain per token compared with full attention.

explainer.example: Serving an RWKV model requires constant memory per token regardless of context length, since no KV cache is kept.
